ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AD is the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle EAC$ of $\triangle ABC$, and AD intersects the circumcircle $O$ of $\triangle ABC$ at point D. $DB = DC$; if $\angle CAB=30^\circ$, and $BC=4$, what is the length of the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{DC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect OB, OC, and OD.\\
By the Circumference Angle Theorem, $\angle COB=2\angle CAB=60^\circ$, $\angle CDB=\angle CAB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle COB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore OC=BC=4$,\\
$\because DC=DB$, $\angle CDB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DCB=75^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DCO=15^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle COD=150^\circ$,\\
Therefore, the length of the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{DC}$ is $= \frac{150\pi \times 4}{180}=\boxed{\frac{10}{3}\pi}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, AD is the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle EAC$ of $\triangle ABC$, and AD intersects the circumcircle $O$ of $\triangle ABC$ at point D. $DB = DC$; if $\angle CAB=30^\circ$, and $BC=4$, what is the length of the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{DC}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect OB, OC, and OD.\\
By the Circumference Angle Theorem, $\angle COB=2\angle CAB=60^\circ$, $\angle CDB=\angle CAB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle COB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore OC=BC=4$,\\
$\because DC=DB$, $\angle CDB=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DCB=75^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DCO=15^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle COD=150^\circ$,\\
Therefore, the length of the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{DC}$ is $= \frac{150\pi \times 4}{180}=\boxed{\frac{10}{3}\pi}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center of the circle labeled O. A is on the right side of the circle, B is at the lower right, C is at the lower left, and D is above and on the circle. On the right side there is a vertical straight line passing through B and A and extending upward to E, so AE is the opposite extension line of AB. The figure draws segments AC, AD, DB, DC, BC, etc.; what is requested is the length of the minor arc from D to C on the circle. Reasoning: It is known that ∠CAB = 30°, and AE is the extension opposite ray of AB, so the exterior angle ∠EAC = 180° - 30° = 150°. AD bisects the exterior angle ∠EAC, therefore ∠DAC = 150°/2 = 75°. ∠DAC is an inscribed angle, and it subtends arc DC not containing A; from the positions of D and C in the figure, this arc is the minor arc, so the central angle corresponding to minor arc DC is 2 × 75° = 150°. Also chord BC corresponds to inscribed angle ∠BAC = 30°, so BC = 2R sin 30° = R. It is known that BC = 4, therefore the circle radius R = 4. Arc length = R × radian measure of central angle = 4 × (150° × π/180°) = 4 × 5π/6 = 10π/3.
